# The Clockwork Harbor

## Chapter One: The Silent Bell

At dawn, courier Mara Venn crossed North Quay with the Brass Gull locked beneath her coat. The mechanical bird clicked once whenever the harbor fog hid a moving ship.

Ivo Rill, an apprentice Tidekeeper, waited beside the dry bell tower. He warned Mara, “If the seventh bell rings, do not answer with your name.”

Mara showed him the copper strip inside the Gull's wing. Etched across it were the words BELL PROTOCOL: RETURN EVERY BORROWED VOICE BEFORE SUNSET. Ivo called it an obsolete emergency rule, but he copied the words into his tide ledger.

## Chapter Two: Borrowed Voices

By noon, every speaking tube in North Quay repeated Mara's name. The Brass Gull tore free from her hands and flew toward the dry bell tower.

Tidekeeper Captain Sera Holt sealed the quay gates. She invoked the Bell Protocol and ordered the Tidekeepers to collect every recorded message before sunset. Ivo admitted that his ledger now answered questions in Mara's voice.

The seventh bell rang without a rope. Mara remained silent. Sera said, “A protocol is a promise made to a disaster.”

## Chapter Three: The Returned Name

At sunset, Mara climbed the dry bell tower while Ivo carried the tide ledger and Sera carried the captured speaking tubes. The Brass Gull perched above the seventh bell.

Mara opened the Gull's copper strip. Ivo read each borrowed message backward, and the harbor returned the stolen voices to their owners. The seventh bell cracked before it could ring again.

Sera retired the Bell Protocol and gave its copper strip to the Tidekeepers' archive. When Mara finally spoke her name, only her own voice answered.
